identity_evidence.quote: A 26-year old woman presented with headache

attribution_limitations: The case narrative and the Figure 3 caption describe a hyperintense lesion on T1-weighted images, while the discussion says hypointensity on T1 for the lipoma; both T1 signal descriptions are kept as review-only source conflicts.

patients.label: Patient 4: 76-year-old patient with headache
attribution_limitations: The narrative cites Fig. 4A for a cystic mass compressing the superior sagittal sinus on T1-weighted MR images, while the Figure 4 caption describes panel A as a sagittal CT image; this panel-modality mismatch is recorded as an ambiguity, not as a patient finding conflict.

The narrative says CT and other imaging suggested an epidermoid tumor, while Table 1 lists Epidermoid cyst in the Diagnosis column without qualification; the condition keeps the narrative certainty (provisional).
The sentence that the tumor location could not result in increased intracranial pressure is the authors reasoning, not a recorded finding for this patient.

The narrative says no surgery was performed because the patient had no clinical symptoms, although the same patient presented with headache; the source does not say whether the headache was considered unrelated to the lesion.

The FLAIR hyperintensity sentence ("The lesions of the two patients of the present series") and the series-level no-malignant-transformation sentence ("In our series ... the patients were managed without surgery") do not name this patient; they are linked to the two epidermoid patients only by paragraph context.

patients.label: Patient 5: 36-year-old man with headache, dysmorphic head appearance and history of tuberous sclerosis
attribution_limitations: The case narrative records a history of tuberous sclerosis, while the discussion sentence about the patient with epidermoid cyst and subependymal giant cell astrocytoma refers to the absence of clinical findings suggestive of tuberous sclerosis; the history fact keeps the case narrative and the discussion negation is review-only.
The narrative places the lesion in the left frontal region while the Figure 5 caption places the expansile lesions in the left frontoparietal region; both are recorded as written.

The narrative says the lesion was interpreted as epidermoid cyst and the caption says the features are consistent with it; Table 1 lists the diagnosis without qualification. The condition keeps provisional certainty.

The FLAIR hyperintensity sentence ("The lesions of the two patients of the present series") and the series-level no-malignant-transformation sentence ("In our series ... the patients were managed without surgery") do not name this patient; they are linked to the two epidermoid patients only by paragraph context.

patients.label: Patient 6: 72-year old woman with headache

identity_evidence.quote: A 72-year old woman presented with headache.

attribution_limitations: Two conflicts for patient 6: (1) lesion laterality is left frontal in the coronal MRI sentence and Figure 6 caption but right frontal in Table 1 localization and the axial T1 and diffusion-weighted sentences; (2) Table 1 (Nonsurgical follow-up) and the Results (dermoid cyst managed conservatively without surgery) contradict the narrative, the dermoid discussion and the Figure 6 caption, which describe total resection with cranioplasty; Table 1 itself also marks a postoperative image (Y). Only the conflicting attributes (side; whether surgery and its pathology occurred) are review-only; signal findings, headache, examination and the dermoid cyst name are included.

patients.label: Patient 7: 70-year-old male patient with headache and occipital soft swelling
attribution_limitations: Discussion paragraph b00117 names "one of our patients" with an arachnoid cyst. The mapping is not literal: the paragraph before it equates intradiploic arachnoid cysts with leptomeningeal cysts, patient 2 (arachnoid/leptomeningeal cyst) has the Table 1 imaging cell "T1 DWI hypointense, T2 DWI hyperintense" that matches its wording, and only the management (no surgery) fits patient 7. The monitoring statements are kept under patient 7 as review-only and are not used in the timeline or summary.
The narrative says the lesion was suggestive of an arachnoid cyst, while Table 1 lists Arachnoid cyst under Diagnosis without qualification; the condition keeps the narrative certainty (provisional).

The Results paragraph says the patient with an arachnoid cyst presented with right parietal swelling; by diagnosis label (Table 1 Arachnoid cyst) this is patient 7, whose narrative swelling is occipital and lesion left occipital, while the right parietal swelling matches patient 2. The sentence is not recorded as a fact for either patient.

identity_evidence.quote: An 18-year old boy presented with persistent headache

attribution_limitations: Patient 9 side of the eosinophilic granuloma: left parietal area in the discussion, but right parietal bone in Table 1, right posterior parietal region in the narrative postoperative CT sentence and the Figure 9 caption; all conflicting sides are review-only.

The narrative gives axial T1 hyperintense and axial FLAIR isointense, while the Figure 9 caption and Table 1 give FLAIR hyperintense and T1 isointense for the same panel letters; this sequence-label mismatch is kept as written and not resolved.
